scientific_conclusion: The full final 1x1 convolution weight has a nonzero pair gradient for every immutable query, and the V65 bias gradients are reproduced exactly. The audit is therefore numerically bound to the same pair problem rather than a changed sampler or query set.

Adding all 480 feature-responsive output weights leaves five of twelve query gradients opposite to the leave-one-out common direction. TNG100 and Swift retain negative domain-median coherence, so a last-layer-only direct pair refit is not supported.
The aggregate pair gradient has a safe scale and is first-order compatible with bounded NLL. Optimization magnitude or a direct NLL conflict is not the reason for rejection.

A single singular direction contains 87.56% of the twelve pair-gradient squared norm. The residual failure is consistent with one dominant nonlocal correction whose sign and amplitude vary by object, motivating a target-free global-context predictability audit before any architectural refit.
